properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 4:12PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Conditions have generally tapered down across Majuro from yesterdays
wind and rain event. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
will bring some locally heavy showers through tonight. Further north,
a tropical disturbance has produced robust convection across Bikini
Atoll and the far northern Marshall Islands today. This morning's
scatterometer shows that gusts could be approaching 40 to 45 knots in
the heaviest showers and thunderstorms. Some of this heavy weather
has made it as far south of Kwajalein today. Over the next couple of
days, model guidance shows a westward shift of the tropical
disturbance with a slow weakening trend. Scattered showers will
remain possible across the RMI this week with a monsoon-like pattern
remaining in place.

Seas could approach 9 to 12 feet where the strongest winds and
heaviest showers occur. This would make conditions hazardous to
Small Craft across the far northern RMI with extreme choppiness.
Boaters moving through the Marshall Islands north of Kwajalein
should practice enhanced caution over the next day or so.

For more information keep up to date with the latest information
from the Majuro Weather Service office and your local emergency
management agency.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the
following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern
Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle
Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin
Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains
including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central
Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De
Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East
Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa
Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands,
Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In
northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast
Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New
Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west
central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and
West Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount
by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along
and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many
locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms
will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour,
and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some
locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6
inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico.  Heavy
rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas,
then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast
to return along and east of the continental divide again on
Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.  Never drive through flood
waters.  Most flash flood deaths occur in automobiles.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 7:14PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
CORRECTED HEADLINE.

...HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE AND PALAU
THROUGH MIDWEEK...
...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES...

An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that
is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to
organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at
times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day
through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the
following few days.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days. Be
aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.
